moat_against: Pure commodity product — no pricing power; OE is set by gas prices, not the company
Reserves deplete: ~$2B+/yr maintenance capex just to hold production flat
Appalachian basis/takeaway constraints and pipeline permitting/regulatory risk
Hedging is light (<10% of 2026 output per commentary) — earnings fully exposed to price swings
moat_for: Lowest-cost Appalachian scale: largest US gas producer, core Marcellus/Utica position
Owned midstream (Equitrans + Mountain Valley Pipeline) cuts gathering/transport cost and basis exposure
Combo-development + compression synergies: FCF-positive at $2.89/MMBtu in Q2 2026
Large proved reserve base and long drilling inventory in the core of the basin
moat_justification: Weak-to-narrow moat (4/10): a real structural cost advantage — largest US natural gas producer, core Marcellus/Utica acreage, owned gathering/transmission midstream after the Equitrans reacquisition (incl. Mountain Valley Pipeline), combo-development drilling and compression synergies that kept Q2 2026 free cash flow positive at $2.89/MMBtu gas — but natural gas is a pure commodity: EQT has no pricing power, earnings are dictated by Henry Hub / regional basis, reserves deplete and must be re-drilled, and takeaway constraints and regulation cap returns. Cost leadership survives a cycle; it does not compound like a wide moat. CAP = 7.2 years.
name: EQT CORPORATION
one_liner: Low-cost integrated gas producer, moat 4/10 — does not clear 15% at $54.80 (weighted IRR 11.6%, weighted IV@15% $39.79) because the TTM base embeds a winter price spike and mid-cycle OE is far lower; clears 15% at ~$39.79.
